newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Anwar says Bakun dam project delayed.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Anwar says Bakun dam project delayed.

text.p: Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday that the $6.18 billion Bakun dam is facing a "slight delay" due to a disagreement between the project's main developer and a key contractor.
"I suppose there might be slight delay...due to the disagreement over the agreement," Anwar told reporters following an Islamic capital market conference.
He characterised the dispute as "major disagreements" between Ekran Bhd and one of the projects two main contractors ABB.
Anwar did not state the expected length of the delay. The project is due to be completed by 2003.
"There has been conflict over the EPC (engineering, procurement and construction) agreement between Ekran and ABB and therefore, it would lead to some delay in the project," Anwar said.
"The dispute is over major terms of the agreement.
"The estimates have been very very conflicting...of the total amount required. We plan to resolve this as soon as possible," he said.
Anwar said the delay in the project was also due to the delay in the diversion tunnel, being built to divert water away from the construction site.
Minister for Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Leo Moggie has been asked to intervene and resolve the issue, he said.
"Not only sub-contracting, I think the main agreement needs to be relooked at," Anwar said, when asked if the dispute was over award of sub-contracts.

ABB's portion of the work on Bakun include supplying six 420 MW hydro-generators, a 500-kilovolt high voltage direct-current transmission system, installing the record setting 650-km (400-mile) long submarine cable to connect the dam to Peninsular Malaysia and civil works with joint contractor, Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos e Obras (CBPO).
Ekran was the company to which the government awarded the contract. It has a 32 percent stake in Bakun Hydroelectric Corp Bhd (BHEC), the operating company of the project.
